target.title: improve: require fresh canonical worktrees for coding agents
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Coding agents can begin PR work in a primary checkout or on a stale local branch, which risks mixing unrelated changes, losing contributor history, or publishing work that was never based on the intended upstream repository.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds one Git work-isolation contract across OpenClaw's full and minimal agent prompts, agent-bundle default and custom prompts, the bundled coding-agent skill, and generated workspace instruction templates. New work must verify the intended PR target and start from a freshly fetched canonical base; existing PR/shared-branch work instead refreshes canonical state while preserving the fetched contributor head and forbidding automatic history rewrites.

The coding-agent skill also requires a truthful preparation receipt that records the preparation mode, actual source ref, starting SHA, isolated worktree, and canonical base before a worker starts editing.

## User Impact

Users delegating implementation work get a consistent fresh-base safety rule regardless of prompt mode or workspace template. Coding agents avoid the primary checkout, stop when the PR target cannot be verified, preserve existing contributor branches, and re-check canonical ancestry before publishing newly authored work.

## Evidence

- AWS Crabbox run `run_e6caacf21353` on the final rebased branch: 103 focused prompt/template tests passed across two Vitest shards.
- The same run passed formatting for all 10 changed files, core and core-test `tsgo`, targeted Oxlint, and `pnpm build`.
- AWS Crabbox run `run_e04c069413f9`: `pnpm prompt:snapshots:check` reported all 7 committed prompt snapshots current.
- Final Codex autoreview against `upstream/main` reported no accepted or actionable findings.
- Final canonical ancestry check passed with branch parent `1aff6da8274c756bc6c30750b701268db1439133` equal to current `upstream/main`.
